Which companies worry about tariffs on i.answer: Several companies in the search results say they worry about tariffs involving China. Apple cites new tariffs on imports from mainland China [1]. Boeing says China is a major market and that tariff negotiations led Chinese customers to pause deliveries [2][3]. Eli Lilly points to 2025 U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods and Chinese retaliation [4]. Amgen flags possible Section 301 tariffs on Chinese imports [5]. Tesla, Intuitive Surgical, and Honeywell also cite tariffs tied to China or U.S.-China trade tensions [6][7][8]. Across all 102 companies, 61 added or expanded tariff and trade language this year, and 5 cut it [9].

How does JPMorgan describe the risk of a.answer: JPMorgan treats cyberattacks as a major operational risk in several parts of its risk factors. Its main cyber risk factor, "A successful cyber attack could cause significant harm to JPMorganChase and its clients and customers," warns that it could become "increasingly vulnerable to cyber attacks" if it does not address emerging threats and software vulnerabilities, including "zero-day vulnerabilities" [1][2]. It also lists concerns such as distributed denial-of-service attacks, ransomware, and insider threats [3][4]. A separate risk says its exposure grows through its links to clients, vendors and other outside parties, since "interconnectivity... continues to expand, which increases the risk of failure or cyber attacks" [5][6]. The company says it has experienced operational failures and expects more, which have included customers being unable to access accounts and the exfiltration of customer personal data [7][8].

Which companies stopped mentioning ESG?.answer: Twenty-six of the 102 companies dropped ESG language from their risk factors entirely this year. They are ADBE, AMGN, AMT, AVGO, AXP, BKNG, CMCSA, CRM, GE, GILD, GS, INTC, INTU, JPM, MDLZ, MET, NOW, PG, QCOM, RTX, TMO, TSLA, TXN, USB, WFC and WMT. Examples of wording that disappeared include Adobe's note that ESG laws "are expanding globally" [1] and American Tower's caution about meeting its ESG goals [2]. Another 34 companies still mention ESG but used it less this year [3].
